title: Iran claims more tankers hit mines in Hormuz as UK agency reports projectile strike off Oman
dek: Iran's Revolutionary Guards say two supertankers are ablaze after hitting mines; no mine strike has been independently confirmed. Iran's drones hit a US base in Kuwait on Wednesday, its army said, and Trump warns Tehran over chemical weapons.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
Iran's army said on Wednesday that its drones had attacked US forces at Ali Al Salem Air Base in Kuwait, its first reported strike on Kuwait since September, and its army chief warned Washington that Iran would respond "more forcefully and without geographical restrictions" if the United States attacked again, according to reports. Kuwait's military said its air defences had responded to hostile drones but did not say where they came from or report any damage.

The attack, which Iranian media described as retaliation for Tuesday's US strike on a Revolutionary Guards missile site on Iran's Qeshm Island, came as a second tanker was hit in the Strait of Hormuz in two days. The UAE's state-owned shipping company ADNOC Logistics & Services said one of its vessels had been attacked while transiting the strait on Tuesday evening, that 11 crew members were injured and that one was unaccounted for.

## Thursday: more mine claims, Trump warning

On Thursday Iran's Revolutionary Guards navy said two more supertankers, which it claimed were being escorted by US jets, had caught fire after striking mines in the southern part of the strait while taking what it called an "unauthorised route", according to reports. As with earlier claims, Iran did not name the ships, and no shipowner, flag state, the UK Maritime Trade Operations centre (UKMTO) or US Central Command had confirmed any mine strike, reports said. Claims on social media that five tankers were ablaze could not be verified.

UKMTO did issue a new warning, dated 18 November, saying an unknown projectile had hit the engine room of an outbound tanker about 6 nautical miles north of Khasab in Oman at 1645 GMT (10.15 pm IST) on Wednesday. It said, citing local authorities, that the crew were safe and accounted for, and that the damage was not yet known. It did not name the ship or say who fired the projectile, and the alert was issued several hours after the event; it was not clear from the warning whether it described a new attack or one already reported.

In an interview broadcast from Shenzhen, US President Donald Trump said there was "indication" that Iran was looking at chemical or biological weapons because the US had shut it out of nuclear weapons, and that "if it does happen, we wipe them out", according to reports. Iran has not responded to the remark. Reports citing unnamed US officials said fresh US strikes on Iran were being considered but that no decision had been taken. Oil prices were little changed: Brent crude was at about $92 a barrel on Thursday morning after falling 1.3 per cent on Wednesday, reports said.

## Wednesday night: Iran says three tankers hit mines

Late on Wednesday Iran's army navy said three oil tankers had caught fire and stopped moving after striking sea mines east of the Strait of Hormuz, according to Iranian state television as cited in reports. It said the ships had entered a restricted area that morning, ignored warnings and switched off their navigation systems. Iran did not name the ships, and there was no independent confirmation; neither the UK Maritime Trade Operations centre nor US Central Command had commented on the claim, reports said. Iranian forces have reported a string of mine strikes in recent weeks, none of them independently verified.

Yemen's Houthis said on Wednesday evening that they had fired cruise missiles at King Khalid International Airport and Riyadh's financial district, according to their military spokesperson Yahya Saree, who cited Saudi strikes in Yemen. There was no immediate Saudi comment on that claim. The US State Department renewed its advice to US citizens in Saudi Arabia and Bahrain to take increased care, and Iran said it was monitoring the arrival in the region of a third US aircraft carrier, the USS Theodore Roosevelt, reports said.

## What each side says

The Iranian army said its drones targeted US Patriot air-defence systems and drone and missile launch pads at the base, according to Iranian state media. There has been no independent confirmation of any damage. Kuwait's foreign ministry condemned the attacks, saying they "threatened the country's security and stability", and said Kuwait reserved the right to take necessary measures, according to reports. Saudi Arabia also condemned the attacks on Kuwait and Bahrain and called for an end to hostilities, reports said.

Bahrain reported fresh Iranian aerial attacks early on Wednesday, issued shelter alerts and later gave the all-clear; its military said it had intercepted several attacks but gave no details of damage. US Central Command has said every Iranian drone launched at Bahrain on Tuesday was intercepted. Iran's army chief, Major General Amir Hatami, warned the US against what he called a "miscalculation", according to Iranian state media.

Separately, a Saudi-led coalition spokesperson said Saudi air defences had intercepted and destroyed a cruise missile fired by Yemen's Houthis at Riyadh, reports said.

## The tanker attack

The UK Maritime Trade Operations centre, run by the Royal Navy, reported that a tanker was hit by an unknown projectile about 13 nautical miles north of Khasab in Oman on Tuesday evening, starting a fire that was later put out, and that the crew had been evacuated. Industry reports identified the ship as the Navig8 Messi, a tanker commercially managed by ADNOC Logistics & Services. ADNOC did not say who attacked the ship or give the nationalities of the crew.

It was the second attack on a merchant ship in the strait this week. On Monday the Panama-flagged LPG tanker Tara Gas was hit; India's Ministry of External Affairs said on Tuesday that 21 of the 24 Indian nationals on board had been brought ashore at Khasab, two were in hospital and one was missing. The ministry's last update, on Tuesday, said the search for the missing Indian sailor was continuing with Omani authorities; there was no further news by early Thursday.

## Background

The United States and Israel launched strikes on Iran in February, killing several senior Iranian leaders including Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei. Talks have stalled despite a memorandum of understanding signed in June, and the US says it is enforcing a naval blockade of Iran's ports on the Gulf and the Gulf of Oman. Qatari and Iranian officials met on Tuesday to discuss proposals to narrow differences between Tehran and Washington, Qatar's foreign ministry spokesperson Majed Al Ansari said, according to reports.

Iran had resumed attacks on US facilities in Bahrain this week after about two months without such incidents. For India, which imports much of its oil and gas through the strait and whose seafarers have been caught up in the attacks, each new round raises the risks for crews and the cost of shipping.

## What happens next

Trump, Xi and Putin met in Shenzhen on Thursday, and their joint declaration stressed "stable energy flows" but did not mention Iran or the strait by name; Chinese state media said the talks covered the Middle East. Iran said on Monday that a regional bloc backed its two-day plan to reopen the strait; Washington has not publicly responded. India's Ministry of External Affairs had given no further update on the missing Indian sailor from the Tara Gas by Thursday evening.
